title: TAPD-Net: A Dual-Enhancement Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection with Channel Attention and a High-Resolution Detection Head
abstract: Tomato fruit detection in greenhouse scenes is affected by small targets, heavy occlusion, and cluttered foliage backgrounds. To improve a lightweight one-stage detector for this scenario, a dual-enhancement framework named TAPD-Net was constructed by combining a lightweight channel attention module with a high-resolution P2 detection head. The channel attention branch adaptively recalibrates discriminative features, while the P2 branch strengthens fine-grained localization of small tomato instances. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset after conversion to YOLO format. A small parameter search was first performed on the dual-enhancement model, and the best setting was then used for ablation experiments including the baseline, w/o P2 head, w/o channel attention, and the full model. Under the same 120-epoch training schedule, the full model achieved the best final ablation mAP@0.5 of 85.03%, compared with 78.98% for the retrained baseline, 84.18% for w/o P2 head, and 82.30% for w/o channel attention. The results indicate that TAPD-Net is the most complete among the tested innovation combinations for an MDPI-style two-innovation study, although the gain in mAP@0.5:0.95 remains limited.

title: CAWI-Net: A Coordinate-Attention and Wise-IoU Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato fruit detection in greenhouse scenes is affected by occlusion, dense distribution, and confusing foliage backgrounds. To investigate whether a lightweight detector can be improved through coordinated feature enhancement and localization-oriented loss reweighting, a dual-enhancement framework named CAWI-Net was constructed by combining a Coordinate Attention module with a Wise-IoU loss. The attention branch strengthens direction-aware channel responses, whereas the Wise-IoU branch adjusts bounding-box regression emphasis during training. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset after conversion to YOLO format. A small parameter analysis was first performed on the full model under a unified training protocol of 450 epochs with an image size of $608 608$. The three full-model trials reached best monitored mAP@0.5 values of 86.83%, 86.04%, and 86.82%, respectively. For cross-scheme screening, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5. Under this reference, the Coordinate-Attention-only model, the Wise-IoU-only model, and the full model achieved best monitored mAP@0.5 values of 85.76%, 85.56%, and 87.62%, respectively. The results indicate that CAWI-Net forms a technically viable two-innovation solution for greenhouse tomato detection, although its ablation narrative remains less concise than that of the finalized fifth scheme.

title: SDD-Net: A SimAM and Decoupled-Adapter Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato fruit detection in greenhouse scenes is affected by foliage occlusion, dense distribution, and ambiguous maturity transitions. To further evaluate a two-innovation lightweight detector after the finalized fifth scheme, a framework named SDD-Net was constructed by combining a parameter-free SimAM attention module with a decoupled pre-detection adapter design. The SimAM branch enhances local contrast-sensitive feature responses, whereas the decoupled adapter branch separates feature adaptation before final prediction. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. A first round of full-model parameter analysis was carried out under the 450-epoch comparison protocol, and a second targeted retuning step was then performed to obtain the best full-model configuration. For cross-scheme screening, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the SimAM-only model achieved 86.48% mAP@0.5 and 55.31% mAP@0.5:0.95, the decoupled-only model achieved 86.46% and 54.76%, and the retuned full model achieved 86.90% and 56.10%, respectively. The results indicate that SDD-Net provides a logically improved fourth-scheme full model and remains a credible backup manuscript candidate under the current screening protocol.

title: CBF-Net: A Coordinate-Attention and BiFPN Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato ripeness detection in greenhouse scenes is challenged by foliage occlusion, dense fruit distribution, and the need for effective cross-scale feature interaction under lightweight deployment constraints. To further screen a two-innovation detector candidate, a framework named CBF-Net was constructed by combining a Coordinate Attention insertion strategy with a BiFPN-style weighted fusion branch. The Coordinate Attention branch strengthens direction-aware feature emphasis, whereas the BiFPN branch improves multi-scale feature refinement after neck fusion. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. For cross-scheme consistency, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the Coordinate-Attention-only model achieved final 82.72% mAP@0.5 and 52.86% mAP@0.5:0.95, the BiFPN-only model achieved 83.36% and 53.05%, and the previously completed full model achieved 80.75% and 51.45%, respectively. However, when the best monitored values are compared at the scheme-screening level, the full model reaches 85.99% mAP@0.5, exceeding the Coordinate-Attention-only model at 85.32% and the BiFPN-only model at 85.36%. These results indicate that CBF-Net remains a usable two-innovation manuscript candidate for project screening, although the full model still requires a stronger final convergence pattern than the best-performing finalized schemes.

title: CBRH-Net: A CBAM and Re-Parameterization Head Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato ripeness detection in greenhouse scenes is affected by dense small fruits, foliage occlusion, and background clutter. To screen a later-stage manuscript candidate under a lightweight detection setting, a framework named CBRH-Net was constructed by combining a CBAM-based feature enhancement strategy with a re-parameterization head branch. The CBAM branch strengthens channel-spatial feature selection under complex greenhouse interference, whereas the re-parameterization head branch aims to improve the adaptability of pre-detection features before prediction. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. For cross-scheme consistency, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the CBAM-only model achieved 83.82% mAP@0.5 and 52.88% mAP@0.5:0.95, the re-parameterization-head-only model achieved 83.58% and 53.52%, and the selected full model achieved 84.57% and 52.34%, respectively. The results indicate that CBRH-Net is a usable mAP@0.5-oriented backup manuscript candidate because both single-innovation variants surpass the shared baseline and the selected full model provides the strongest final mAP@0.5 among the seventh-scheme variants.

title: MDY-Net: A MLCA and DySample Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato ripeness detection in greenhouse scenes is affected by dense small fruits, leaf occlusion, and the need to preserve detailed multi-scale representation in lightweight detectors. To screen a later-stage backup manuscript candidate, a framework named MDY-Net was constructed by combining a mixed local channel attention (MLCA) insertion strategy with a DySample upsampling branch. The MLCA branch enhances lightweight channel-aware feature emphasis, whereas the DySample branch replaces fixed upsampling with dynamic sampling-based feature reconstruction. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. For cross-scheme consistency, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the MLCA-only model achieved final 85.25% mAP@0.5 and 54.82% mAP@0.5:0.95, the DySample-only model achieved 83.49% and 53.24%, and the previously completed full model achieved 83.14% and 52.22%, respectively. However, when the best monitored values are compared for screening purposes, the full model reaches 86.38% mAP@0.5, exceeding the MLCA-only model at 86.25% and the DySample-only model at 85.57%. The results indicate that MDY-Net can be organized as a best-monitored screening-style two-innovation candidate, although its final recorded metrics remain less concise than those of the stronger finalized schemes.

title: SDY-Net: A SPPELAN and Dynamic-Head Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato ripeness detection in greenhouse scenes remains difficult because of foliage occlusion, adjacent maturity states, and the need for precise small-object recognition under lightweight deployment constraints. To screen a late-stage backup manuscript candidate, a framework named SDY-Net was constructed by combining an SPPELAN replacement strategy with a dynamic pre-detection head branch. The SPPELAN branch replaces the original spatial pyramid aggregation module, whereas the dynamic-head branch introduces adaptive feature refinement before final prediction. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. A first round of full-model parameter analysis was performed under the 450-epoch comparison protocol, and the resulting settings were then followed by completed ablation runs. For cross-scheme screening, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the SPPELAN-only model achieved 79.76% mAP@0.5 and 50.48% mAP@0.5:0.95, the dynamic-head-only model achieved 82.56% and 52.58%, and the full model achieved 82.71% and 52.97%, respectively. The results indicate that SDY-Net remains usable as a screening-style two-innovation candidate because the combined model surpasses the shared baseline reference and yields the strongest final result among the completed ninth-scheme variants, although the overall gain remains moderate.

title: SCAR-Net: A SimAM and CARAFE Enhanced Framework for Tomato Ripeness Detection
abstract: Tomato ripeness detection in greenhouse scenes is influenced by partial leaf occlusion, dense fruit distribution, and the need to preserve small-object details in lightweight detectors. To screen a later-stage backup manuscript candidate, a framework named SCAR-Net was constructed by combining a backbone SimAM attention insertion strategy with a CARAFE upsampling branch. The SimAM branch strengthens locally informative responses without adding convolutional parameters, while the CARAFE branch replaces fixed nearest-neighbor upsampling with content-aware feature reconstruction. Experiments were conducted on the TomatOD dataset in YOLO format. A first round of full-model parameter analysis was performed under the 450-epoch comparison protocol, and the resulting setting was then used in the completed ablation runs. For cross-scheme screening, the common baseline reference from the finalized fifth scheme was retained at 78.98% mAP@0.5 and 50.69% mAP@0.5:0.95. Under this reference, the SimAM-only model achieved 85.26% mAP@0.5 and 54.55% mAP@0.5:0.95, the CARAFE-only model achieved 78.44% and 49.61%, and the full model achieved 85.66% and 53.83%, respectively. The results indicate that SCAR-Net is a usable mAP@0.5-oriented two-innovation candidate because the combined model produces the strongest final mAP@0.5 among the screened tenth-scheme variants, although the CARAFE branch alone does not surpass the shared baseline and the strict mAP@0.5:0.95 metric remains slightly below the SimAM-only model.

title: TeaNet: A Lightweight Dual-Attention YOLO Model for Multi-Class Tea Leaf Disease Detection
direction: 茶叶叶片多类病害检测
abstract: % Accurate detection of tea leaf diseases is essential for precision agriculture and early intervention in tea plantations. Existing lightweight detectors often struggle with fine-grained discrimination among visually similar disease categories and with detecting small early-stage lesions. To address these challenges, this work proposes TeaNet, a dual-innovation YOLO-based framework built on YOLO11n. The first innovation, C2f-MLCA, replaces all C2f blocks with a mixed local channel attention variant that enhances discriminative feature responses across backbone and neck without significant parameter overhead. The second innovation, DyHeadAdapter, introduces a dynamic detection head that unifies scale, spatial, and task attention before the final prediction layer, improving multi-scale sensitivity for small lesion detection. Experiments were conducted on a tea leaf disease dataset comprising 9,591 images across eight disease categories with a train/valid/test split. Under a unified training protocol of 100 epochs at $640 640$ resolution, TeaNet achieved a best mAP@0.5 of TBD% on the held-out test split, outperforming the YOLO11n baseline by TBD% and surpassing representative comparison methods. Ablation results confirm that both innovations contribute independently and synergistically. The proposed model provides an effective and deployable solution for automated tea disease monitoring.%
